skill.name: code-simplification
skill.description: Guides behavior-preserving code simplification through context gathering, focused refactoring, incremental testing, and final verification.
skill.summary: A practical workflow for making code easier to understand without changing its behavior.
skill.author: addyosmani

security_audit.summary: All 26 external-command findings are false positives caused by shell-like backticks in Markdown examples and inline code. The hardcoded URL is a documentation reference, and the five reconnaissance findings describe ordinary scope and verification practices; no malicious intent or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Static analysis interprets Markdown code fences and inline backticks as Ruby or shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Improve the scanner to distinguish Markdown fences and inline code from executable Ruby or shell syntax, or annotate documentation-only examples.

remediation.issue: The skill includes a hardcoded URL to the upstream inspiration document.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the link limited to documentation context and verify that it remains an intended, trusted reference during source updates.

content.value_statement: Complex code slows reviews, maintenance, and debugging. This skill guides focused refactoring that improves clarity while preserving behavior, errors, side effects, and tests.
actual_capabilities: Identify nested logic, long functions, duplication, unclear names, and unnecessary abstractions.
Compare code context, conventions, tests, callers, and error paths before suggesting a change.
Recommend guard clauses, focused helpers, clearer names, and simpler data transformations.
Organize refactoring into small, reviewable steps with tests after each change.
Check the final result for preserved behavior, project consistency, and unintended scope expansion.
limitations: It cannot prove behavior preservation without suitable tests and enough project context.
It provides guidance for an AI coding agent and does not itself edit or execute repository files.
It should not replace performance analysis when a simplification may affect critical hot paths.
It may defer changes when the code purpose, conventions, or edge cases are unclear.

use_cases.title: Clean Up a Recent Feature
use_cases.description: Review recently changed code for unnecessary nesting, duplication, and unclear names while keeping the feature behavior unchanged.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Safer Code Review
use_cases.description: Turn a broad readability concern into small refactoring steps, explicit checks, and a focused reviewable diff.

use_cases.title: Reduce Legacy Complexity
use_cases.description: Understand an older module before simplifying it, preserving error paths, side effects, project conventions, and existing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Find Simple Improvements
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this function for readability issues. Identify the smallest behavior-preserving improvements and explain why each one helps.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify With Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this module and its tests. Propose one simplification at a time, describe the preserved behavior, and specify the test to run after each step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused refactoring of a tested module

prompt_templates.title: Respect Project Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Study the surrounding code and project conventions before reviewing this change. Suggest clarity improvements that match existing naming, error handling, and module patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this refactoring candidate deeply. Trace callers, side effects, error paths, edge cases, tests, and historical constraints, then produce a staged plan with explicit stop conditions.

output_examples.input: A function uses four nested conditionals to validate input, permission, and state.
output_examples.output: Recommend ordered guard clauses with one validation per step. Explain that the change should preserve exception types, messages, and successful results.

output_examples.input: A pull request mixes a new feature with a broad cleanup of nearby modules.
output_examples.output: Recommend separating the feature and cleanup into independent changes. Identify unrelated files as scope expansion and request tests for each focused refactor.

output_examples.input: A helper appears redundant, but its callers and historical purpose are unclear.
output_examples.output: Defer removal until callers, tests, project conventions, and history are understood. Record the missing evidence instead of guessing.

best_practices: Understand responsibility, callers, edge cases, error paths, tests, and project conventions before changing code.
Make one focused simplification at a time and run the relevant tests after each step.
Judge success by comprehension and preserved behavior, not by line count alone.
anti_patterns: Do not simplify code you do not understand or remove error handling because it appears verbose.
Do not combine unrelated feature work with a broad refactoring pass.
Do not replace tested project conventions with personal style preferences without evidence.

faq.question: What does this skill simplify?
faq.answer: It targets nesting, long functions, duplication, unclear names, redundant abstractions, and other readability problems.

faq.question: Does it change program behavior?
faq.answer: The intended outcome preserves inputs, outputs, side effects, ordering, errors, edge cases, and existing tests.

faq.question: Does it edit files automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides a process for an AI coding agent. The agent decides whether to propose or apply edits in the active workflow.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the relevant code, tests, project conventions, callers, and any performance or compatibility constraints.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the code is not understood, tests are insufficient, performance is critical, or a full rewrite is already planned.

faq.question: How does it reduce refactoring risk?
faq.answer: It favors narrow scope, incremental changes, explicit reasoning, test runs, and a final review of behavior and diff quality.
